newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti's CEO confirms sell-off plan.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti's CEO confirms sell-off plan.

text.p: Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colaninno confirmed his plan to sell off a string of businesses in a rescue plan for the troubled high-tech group in a meeting with Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani on Thursday.

"The meeting with the minister was a good opportunity to explain our strategy, to say what we mean by being in the IT sector and what we mean by sell-offs...to combine strategic and financial needs," he told reporters after the meeting.

Colaninno last week announced his plan to sell off four units including the loss-making personal computer company by the end of this year. He promised to nurse the company back to profit by 1998, saying Olivetti's future lay in its telecommunication interests.

Bersani has been critical of the sell-off plan, particularly the sale of the PC business. "Captains of industry should not abandon ship...to save themselves on a portable phone liferaft," he was quoted as saying at the weekend.
Asked by reporters what Bersani had said on this subject during the meeting, Colaninno said, "ask him, perhaps he has changed his mind."
In reply to a question about the current state of negotiations for the sale of the PC business, he said, "we are discussing it but I can't say who with."
Olivetti shares eased in Milan on Wednesday after an early rise after Japanese companies NEC Corp and Sony denied Italian press reports they were interested in buying the PC business.
Olivetti closed on Thursday 1.11 percent down at 510 lire.
